title: Minimum Total Cost to Process All Elements
summary: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, you start with k resources.
statement: Given an integer array nums and an integer k, you start with k resources. Process each element of nums from left to right, where each element requires a certain number of resources. If your resources are insufficient, you can increase them by k at a cost, with the cost of each operation increasing sequentially. After processing each element, your resources decrease by the element's value. Return the minimum total cost modulo 10^9 + 7.
constraints: Start with k resources and process nums from left to right.
Before an item, buy k more resources as often as necessary; the j-th purchase costs j.
After processing, subtract the item requirement, flooring remaining resources at zero. Return minimum total cost modulo 1,000,000,007.
hints: When current resources are short, buy the smallest whole number of k-sized blocks that covers the deficit.
Ceiling division computes that count directly.
Only the total number of purchases matters because their costs are 1,2,...
Greedy minimum purchases at each forced deficit gives the global count and triangular cost.
editorial: Greedy minimum purchases at each forced deficit gives the global count and triangular cost.

tests.explanation: Two purchases are necessary across the sequence and cost one plus two, totaling three.
The initial resources cover the item, so no purchase is needed.
